nieuw.titel: Include control to buy Wood Elves time
nieuw.tekst: Include an element of control to slow the opponent and create space for favourable strikes, rather than simply trading units.
nieuw.waarom: He says Wood Elves usually need to buy time to win and find an advantage before striking.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He makes an exception for Wild Hunt, which can run straight at the opponent.

bronnen.citaat: you need an element of control in your faction some way or the other

extraCitaten.citaat: You can't just kind of trade as a wood elf player.

nieuw.titel: Try a level-four Spellweaver on a Warhawk
nieuw.tekst: He highly recommends a level-four Spellweaver on a Warhawk with Heartwood Pendant and Oaken Stave for battlefield control and magic defence. He prefers Lore of the Wilds through the pendant, but also considers Battle Magic or Elementalism viable alternatives; Ruby Ring is optional.
nieuw.waarom: He values the combination of Evasive, flight and skirmishing for safe positioning, and Oaken Stave for defending against key enemy spells.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says its magic defence will not match armies with exceptional casting bonuses, although it can compete with an ordinary level-four wizard.

bronnen.citaat: a spellw weaver level four on a warhawk.

extraCitaten.citaat: Ruby ring is probably optional but I wouldn't go home without the rest.
against your run-of-the-mill level four who just gets plus two

nieuw.titel: Use Tree Singing to extend a defensive forest
nieuw.tekst: With the mobile Warhawk wizard, consider Tree Singing to extend an existing forest in your deployment area and block line of sight. Place it outside the opponent's dispel range when possible.
nieuw.waarom: He says the wizard's mobility helps it reach the needed position safely, and that Tree Singing can have an enormous effect when the opponent fails to dispel it.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He acknowledges that the opponent will often dispel Tree Singing.

bronnen.citaat: cast tree singing to create an extra long forest attached to another forest

nieuw.titel: Consider a lesser wizard with Lore Familiar
nieuw.tekst: Consider accompanying the Warhawk control wizard with a lesser wizard carrying Lore Familiar to secure the spells you want.
nieuw.waarom: He points out that the Warhawk build does not have Lore Familiar.

bronnen.citaat: a lesser wizard that has law familiar to get the spells you want.

nieuw.titel: Prefer ten or twenty Glade Guard
nieuw.tekst: He prefers building Glade Guard into units of ten or twenty rather than leaving the compulsory Grand Army unit at five.
nieuw.waarom: He describes Glade Guard as damage dealers rather than merely a five-model roadblock, and notes that they also score.

bronnen.citaat: I think they're actually best placed when you have 10 of them or 20

extraCitaten.citaat: Glade Guard is your damage dealer.

nieuw.titel: Keep Deepwood Scouts around ten models
nieuw.tekst: He thinks ten models is the sweet spot for Deepwood Scouts, rather than building them like the larger Glade Guard units.
nieuw.waarom: He gives them a distraction role and says opponents often dislike chasing ten elves.

bronnen.citaat: I think you only really want to take 10

nieuw.titel: Give damage-dealing Glade Guard Arcane Bodkins
nieuw.tekst: He recommends Arcane Bodkins for Glade Guard used as damage dealers.
nieuw.waarom: In his view, this unit needs to deal damage to fulfil its role.

nieuw.titel: Consider Trueflight Arrows for moving Deepwood Scouts
nieuw.tekst: He thinks Trueflight Arrows are a slightly better fit for Deepwood Scouts that move and shoot while distracting the opponent.
nieuw.waarom: He says their main job is not dealing damage; occasional chip wounds are a good result.

nieuw.titel: Keep Glade Guard distant and withdraw off the hill
nieuw.tekst: Keep Glade Guard as far away as possible and stationary while shooting. When the enemy gets close enough, drop off the hill to make reaching them take another turn.
nieuw.waarom: He warns that pushing Glade Guard forward like Evasive Deepwood Scouts leaves them vulnerable to being destroyed, particularly by Fireball.

nieuw.titel: Use Deepwood Scouts to waste an opponent's turns
nieuw.tekst: Use Deepwood Scouts as mobile distractions, repeatedly moving and shooting while making the opponent chase them. He suggests hiding them in a forest and using Evasive to leave it.
nieuw.waarom: He says their role is distraction rather than dealing substantial damage, and opponents often do not want to chase ten elves.

nieuw.titel: Keep Glade Riders and Warhawk Riders out of combat
nieuw.tekst: Do not treat Glade Riders' cavalry spears as a reason to put them into combat. He gives the same warning for Warhawk Riders.
nieuw.waarom: He says Wood Elf units have tightly defined roles and are punished when used outside those roles.

nieuw.titel: Place Woodland Ambush to create a sheltered corridor
nieuw.tekst: Consider placing Woodland Ambush between a hill and impassable terrain to create a sheltered corridor behind them. In his experience, the extra forest generally works best in or just outside your deployment zone.
nieuw.waarom: He uses this space to hide units, manoeuvre towards the enemy backline and shelter units that may need to Evade into it.

nieuw.titel: Move Wood Elves into the space you clear
nieuw.tekst: When you clear one side of the board, move into that open ground rather than remaining stationary. Keep shifting towards the opponent's deployment zone as the enemy chases you.
nieuw.waarom: He says punching through and relocating forces the opponent to split its forces, making it harder to kill the whole Wood Elf army.
